title: Nested Loops
goal: This lesson covers how to visit every cell in a 2D list with a loop inside another loop.
learn: The outer loop picks each row
The inner loop visits each item in that row
idea: To visit every cell you need nested loops. The outer loop picks each row, and the inner loop goes through every item in that row. Together they reach every cell, going left to right and then down to the next row, a bit like reading a tiny table.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change print(cell) to print("cell:", cell) and press Run. Each line should start with cell:.

practice.text: Use nested loops to print every number in the grid.
practice.hint: The outer loop picks each row. The inner loop visits every cell in that row and prints it.
practice.starterTip: Try: for row in grid: then inside it, for cell in row: and print(cell).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if nested loops print all nine numbers.

practice.text: Visit every cell and print only the ones that are greater than 5.
practice.hint: Keep your nested loops, but only print when the cell is bigger than 5. Use if cell > 5:
practice.starterTip: Inside for cell in row:, add if cell > 5: then print(cell) indented under the if.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if nested loops print 6, 7, 8, and 9 only.

quiz.question: What does the outer loop usually loop over?
quiz.correct: Right, the outer loop walks through the rows.
quiz.wrong: for row in grid picks each inner list.

quiz.question: What does the inner loop do?

options.text: Visits each cell in the current row

quiz.correct: Yes, the inner loop walks left to right across one row.
quiz.wrong: for cell in row visits every value in that row.

quiz.question: How many times does the inner body run on a 3x3 grid?
quiz.correct: Right, 3 rows with 3 cells each means 9 visits.
quiz.wrong: Every cell is visited once, so that is nine times in total.

project.title: Visit Every Seat
project.desc: Use nested loops to print every name in a 3x3 seating chart with the word Hello.
